title: Review: Stationary waves and harmonics; Sound; Superposition, interference and coherence; Intensity; Reflection and refraction
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W06-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W12-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W04-1#N.9a, W06-1#N.8, W10-uk1#N.10, W12-1#N.13, W17-1#N.4, W04-1#N.6a, W06-1#N.2a, W12-1#N.2, W06-1#N.12, W06-1#N.9. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ray
items.clue: Line perpendicular to the wavefronts, showing the direction the energy travels.

items.label: Antiphase
items.clue: Relation between two sources that adds π everywhere, turning every maximum into a minimum.

items.label: Intensity
items.clue: Power arriving per unit area on a surface perpendicular to the wave's direction, in W m⁻².

items.label: Refraction
items.clue: Change in direction as a transmitted wave changes speed on crossing a boundary at an angle.

questions.stem: A ray of light passes from air into a transparent liquid. The incident ray makes an angle of 40.0° with the surface of the liquid and the refracted ray makes an angle of 55.0° with the surface. The speed of light in air is 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What is the speed of light in the liquid?

Two loudspeakers connected to the same signal generator emit sound in phase at a frequency of 500 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m s⁻¹. At which of these path differences is the sound quiet because of destructive interference?
questions.explanation: λ = 0.68 m, and 1.02 m = 1.5λ, a half-odd number of wavelengths: crest meets trough, destructive.

questions.stem: A loudspeaker emitting a 1000 Hz note faces a hard wall. A microphone moved along the line between them detects positions of minimum loudness 0.17 m apart. What is the speed of sound?

options.text: 170 m s⁻¹
340 m s⁻¹
85 m s⁻¹
680 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Node to node = λ/2, so λ = 0.34 m. v = fλ = 1000 × 0.34 = 340 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A small source sends out sound equally in all directions. At 2.0 m from the source the intensity is 6.0 × 10⁻³ W m⁻². Ignoring reflections and absorption, what is the intensity 3.0 m from the source?

A student at one end of a long steel railway track puts an ear to the rail. At the other end, 1.0 km away, the rail is struck once with a hammer. The student hears two separate sounds, 0.20 s and 2.9 s after the blow. Which conclusion do these observations support?

options.text: Sound is slowed by closely packed particles: the first sound came through the air.
Sound has one fixed speed, so the second sound was an echo of the first sound.
Sound travels faster in steel than in air: the first sound came through the rail.
The blow pushed steel along the rail to the ear, so the sound through the rail came first.

questions.stem: The refractive index of a certain plastic is 1.5. Which statement correctly describes what this value means?

options.text: Light travels 1.5 times as fast in the plastic as in a vacuum.
The plastic's density is 1.5 times the density of water.
A ray entering from air is bent to 1/1.5 of its angle of incidence.
Light travels 1.5 times as fast in a vacuum as it does in the plastic.

questions.stem: Two pulses of identical shape and size but opposite displacement travel towards each other along a stretched string. At one instant they overlap exactly and the whole string is momentarily straight. Which statement about this instant, and what follows it, is correct?

options.text: The pulses have cancelled each other out; the string stays straight from now on.
The string is straight but moving; the pulses then emerge and continue past each other.
The string is straight and at rest; the pulses' energy has become internal energy of the string.
The pulses have collided; each then travels back the way it came, with its shape restored.

questions.stem: Sunlight of intensity 1.0 × 10³ W m⁻² falls perpendicularly on a flat solar cell of area 150 cm². At what rate does the sunlight deliver energy to the cell?

Two dippers vibrating in phase act as coherent sources S₁ and S₂ on a ripple tank, producing waves of wavelength 2.0 cm. Point P is 31.0 cm from S₁ and 37.0 cm from S₂. What kind of interference occurs at P?

options.text: Destructive: the paths are 15.5λ and 18.5λ, not whole numbers of λ
Destructive: the path difference, 3λ, is an odd number of λ
Neither: maxima occur only where P is equidistant from S₁ and S₂
Constructive: the path difference is 6.0 cm, which is 3λ

questions.stem: Two loudspeakers side by side are driven by two separate signal generators, each set to 500 Hz. A listener walking across the room hears no steady pattern of loud and quiet places. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Sound waves from two different sources pass through each other without superposing.
A steady pattern forms only if the listener is the same distance from both speakers.
The phase difference drifts, as two generators never match frequency exactly.
Sources must emit at exactly the same amplitude, and two speakers never do.

questions.explanation: Separate generators differ slightly in frequency, so the phase difference keeps changing and the loud and quiet places move. The sources are not coherent.
